html:
Belmopan is the capital of Belize, a planned town built in the interior in the 1960s and made the seat of government in 1970.

After Hurricane Hattie flooded Belize City in 1961, the government of British Honduras chose a site about 80 kilometres inland, safe from storm surges, on the road to Guatemala. Its government buildings were laid out around a central square, with the National Assembly in a building shaped like a Maya temple.

Belmopan grew slowly. Belize City stayed the biggest town and the centre of trade, and for decades many civil servants commuted rather than move. It is still one of the smallest capitals in the Americas. Like Brasília, it was an attempt to move a country's centre of gravity inland, on the scale of Belize.
sum: Belmopan is the capital of Belize, a planned town built in the interior in the 1960s and made the seat of government in 1970.
